subject: FY26 Community Preservation Act Project Presentations
overview: The committee heard presentations for six projects seeking Community Preservation Act funding for the FY26 round, spanning historic preservation, open space, and affordable housing. No final funding decisions were made during this session, with deliberations scheduled for December.

items.title: Angel of Victory and Peace Fountain Restoration
items.summary: Veterans Affairs Director Veronica Shaw presented a $193,000 request to restore the internal filtration and external drainage systems of the historic fountain at Oak Grove Cemetery.

items.title: Shiloh Baptist Church Stained Glass Restoration
items.summary: Representatives from Shiloh Baptist Church requested $150,000 for the first phase of restoring a historic Palladian window and adjacent stained glass to address heat loss and structural decay. The committee requested an updated budget and weatherization recommendations from the project architect.

items.title: Riverside Plaza Shade Improvements Additional Funding
items.summary: City Planner Amanda Centrella presented a revised design and requested $125,000 in additional contingency funding after initial construction bids for the shade project significantly exceeded original estimates. The committee discussed the necessity of an expedited decision to meet state grant deadlines.

items.title: Playstead Park Digital Scoreboard
items.summary: Medford High School Baseball Coach Orazio Azzarello requested $110,000 for a digital scoreboard at Playstead Park to modernize the facility and facilitate tournament revenue. The committee suggested the applicant seek private fundraising matches to supplement the public grant.

items.title: Carriage House Restoration and Affordable Housing ADU
items.summary: Homeowners Kevin Simon and Hilary White requested $235,000 to restore a historic carriage house and convert it into a deed-restricted affordable accessory dwelling unit. The committee discussed the administrative complexity of monitoring a single-unit private residence for long-term affordability.

items.title: Oak Grove Cemetery Buildings Preservation
items.summary: DPW Commissioner Tim McGivern provided an update on the $6.24 million preservation of cemetery structures and introduced an alternative to build a new operational facility while maintaining the historic stone building as a monument. The committee noted the high cost of the preservation bond and requested further clarity on the cemetery's long-term strategic plan.

items.title: Administrative Updates
items.summary: The committee discussed potential tabling at a local community event and noted that the COVID-19 memorial project presentation was postponed to the November meeting.
